result.headline: You have $3,000.00 in credit card debt at 24.00% APR with a $6,000.00 limit (50.00% utilization). Only $185.00 is available after bills, minimums, buffer, and goal savings are reserved. Paying the full $185.00 extra toward the card first reduces interest by $253.50 and pays it off about 5 months sooner than paying only the $100.00 minimum.

findings.summary: Credit card balance of $3,000.00 at 24.00% APR; minimum payment is $100.00 due 2026-11-20.
Card utilization is 50.00% ($3,000.00 balance against a $6,000.00 limit).
Baseline payoff at $100.00/month takes 47 months and costs $1,627.30 in interest.
Applying the full available $185.00 extra to the card (debt-first) costs $1,373.80 in interest, saves $253.50, and pays off in 42 months (est. 2030-04-20).
Goal-first allocation puts $185.00 toward the purchase goal with no interest reduction; debt payoff remains 47 months (est. 2030-09-20).
Balanced allocation splits $185.00 ($92.50 debt, $92.50 goal), costing $1,495.73 in interest, saving $131.57, and paying off in 45 months (est. 2030-07-20).

findings.summary: Debt-first option: apply $185.00 extra to the credit card. Total interest $1373.80, saving $253.50 vs baseline, debt-free est. 2030-04-20. Car goal remains at $500.00 saved with $2500.00 remaining; no new goal contribution this period.
Goal-first option: contribute $185.00 to the car goal. Car goal saved rises to $685.00 with $2315.00 remaining. Debt payoff remains baseline: $1627.30 interest, debt-free est. 2030-09-20.

Balanced option: split $185.00 as $92.50 extra debt and $92.50 goal contribution. Total interest $1495.73, saving $131.57 vs baseline, debt-free est. 2030-07-20. Car goal saved rises to $592.50 with $2407.50 remaining.

Budget snapshot: $3000.00 starting cash, $2815.00 reserved (bills $1215.00, minimum payment $100.00, buffer $1000.00, existing goal savings $500.00), $185.00 available. Projected closing cash after obligations and buffer is $1500.00 under all options.

Car savings goal: target $3000.00, $500.00 already saved, $2500.00 remaining, deadline 2027-11-07 (12 months away). No option meets the deadline now; future monthly contributions are estimates, not promises.

result.headline: A $2000.00 surprise expense reduced available cash from $2185.00 to $185.00. The accepted balanced plan (version 1) is retained unchanged; a proposed version 2 scales both extra debt and goal contribution to $92.50 each.

findings.summary: Surprise expense of $2000.00 on checking account moved snapshot from version 1 to version 2. Starting cash fell from $5000.00 to $3000.00; available discretionary cash fell from $2185.00 to $185.00.

Proposed plan version 2 (balanced) vs accepted version 1: extra debt drops from $1092.50 to $92.50 (-$1000.00), goal contribution drops from $1092.50 to $92.50 (-$1000.00), total accounted drops from $5000.00 to $3000.00 (-$2000.00), estimated interest rises from $554.13 to $1495.73, debt-free date moves from 2028-11-20 to 2030-07-20.
